sections.html:
Twin Falls sits on a broad plain along the south rim of the Snake River Canyon in south-central Idaho, and it is the seat of Twin Falls County. No city within 100 miles in the Magic Valley is bigger. The canyon bounds it on the north and divides it from Jerome County.

About 20 square miles hold 51,807 people from the 2020 census, and an estimate of 56,216 for July 1, 2025. Food processing and agriculture remain the economic base. Job moves are a frequent reason for a fast sale. Say you accepted work elsewhere and now carry two payments: closing on your own schedule may be worth more than holding out for the last dollar.

Planners laid out the town in 1904, and it became a village on April 12, 1905. Water made it possible: I. B. Perrine launched the Twin Falls Land and Water Company in 1900, and Milner Dam, completed in 1905, opened up irrigation beyond the canyon. In 1907 the city became seat of the newly created county. The same project gave rise to Kimberly, Buhl, Filer, Hansen and Murtaugh.

Expect to see it in title reports and on older lots, in the form of canal easements, water records and early to mid twentieth century houses. A ditch, canal or shared water right on your parcel is worth mentioning to buyers early. The title company can tell you what is on record.

No other Idaho city this large lacks a direct Interstate connection. U.S. Route 30 and U.S. Route 93 run through, and drivers cross the canyon on the Perrine Bridge to reach Interstate 84, about 5 miles north in Jerome County. State Highway 74 leads south from downtown toward Hollister and Rogerson and on to Jackpot, Nevada. A public transit service runs within city limits.

Commuters to Jerome or along I-84 care which side of the canyon a house is on. Put highway access in your description.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Bills go out from the county by the fourth Monday in November. Pay the first half by December 20 and the second by June 20 of the next year. Address changes go through the Assessor's Office at (208) 735-4870.

  • Miss December 20 on the first half and a 2 percent late charge is added.
  • Interest follows from January 1, at 12 percent a year or 1 percent a month.
  • After June 20 the second half gets the same 2 percent charge, with interest reaching back to January 1.
  • Mail goes to P.O. Box 88, Twin Falls, ID 83303-0088, and needs a postmark no later than the due date.
  • Paying online by card adds a 2.5 percent convenience fee, while an e-check is $2.00. The county keeps none of either.

After a refinance in particular, confirm whether your lender pays the tax. The loan documents will say, or you can ask the lender or title company. Under Idaho Code 63-902(9), a notice that never arrived does not cancel the tax. Call 208-736-4008 about a missing bill or a recent purchase.

On the closing statement, the title company normally splits this year's tax between seller and buyer, while any older unpaid balance is taken from your proceeds. Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer before agreeing to an offer.

Behind on the December and June installments? A sale pays the balance out of proceeds, so the 2 percent charge and monthly interest stop piling up. Choosing the closing date lets you land ahead of the next deadline.

The city's zoning map lets you search by address, and City Code ties setbacks to the zoning designation. Planning and Zoning answers at (208) 735-7267 and Building Safety at (208) 735-7238.

Anything over 200 square feet, such as a shed or other accessory building, calls for both a Zoning Use Permit and a building permit. A shop, garage or addition built without them can draw a flag from a buyer's lender or inspector. Cash buyers skip the lender step, but you should still disclose what you built.

Collect the following before you list:

  • Zoning label and any recorded easements.
  • Permit history for additions, garages and sheds.
  • Latest property tax notice and Treasurer balance.
  • The lease, if a tenant lives there.

Closing follows the usual Idaho path, without a lender. Describe the house, get a written offer and make your call. The title company records the deed, clears liens and settles tax.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is and charges you no fees, commissions or closing costs. A declined offer costs nothing. No price is quoted until we know the house.

sections.h2: Selling a house with repairs or tenants
sections.html:
A house with a worn roof, tired heating or old plumbing usually draws repair requests after a buyer's inspection. A cash buyer looks at the same problems and folds them into the price. Walk through the house with a notepad, list what is wrong, and share it. A buyer who hears about a problem from you trusts the rest of what you say.

If tenants live in the house, the lease matters as much as the condition. Know the end date, the rent and any deposit you hold, and decide whether the buyer will take the house with tenants or empty. Owners who no longer want to manage a rental often find that a sale with the lease attached is the simplest exit.

Once you agree to a price, the title company orders the records, confirms who owns the property and prepares the closing statement. You sign, the liens and tax are paid from the proceeds, and the rest goes to you.

• Inherited houses whose heirs live out of state and must first confirm who can sign.
  • Homes with deferred maintenance on the roof, heating or plumbing.
  • Rentals whose owner is tired of managing tenants.
  • Owners who have fallen behind on a mortgage or the December and June tax installments.

Each starts differently. With an inheritance, gather the death certificate and any court paperwork first. With tax trouble, ask the Treasurer for the exact balance. With a house that needs lots of repair, write down every problem so a buyer can price it. If more than one applies, handle the tax balance first, since it grows. Nothing here is legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: When are Twin Falls County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due by December 20 and half by the next June 20. Bills are sent by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the December 20 payment in Twin Falls County?
faqs.a: The unpaid first half gets a 2 percent late charge, and interest of 12 percent a year starts on January 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Twin Falls?
faqs.a: Over 200 square feet, an accessory building needs a Zoning Use Permit plus a building permit. Confirm for your lot with Planning and Zoning at (208) 735-7267.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Twin Falls house that is not in good shape?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash Home Buyers buys as-is, so repairs come first on nobody's list. You can still list with an agent, though the inspection may bring repair requests.

faqs.q: Is Twin Falls on an interstate?
faqs.a: No. You reach Interstate 84 by crossing the canyon on the Perrine Bridge, about 5 miles north, which makes Twin Falls the largest Idaho city off the Interstate System.
